es: Distinguir en una discusión familiar las frases que acusan, las que describen hechos y los mensajes en primera persona, y encontrar la queja de fondo.

teaching.en: You always ignore me at family dinners, and whenever I bring up a problem you simply brush off my worries.
teaching.es: Siempre me ignoras en las cenas familiares y, cada vez que saco un problema, simplemente le quitas importancia a mis preocupaciones.
teaching.explanationEs: Acusación: always y simply brush off juzgan a la persona en lugar de contar un hecho.
segments: You always ignore me at family dinners, and whenever I
bring up a problem you simply brush off my worries.
teaching.audioText: You always ignore me at family dinners, and whenever I bring up a problem you simply brush off my worries.

teaching.en: A neutral description only states what anyone could see: the sink was full of dishes again when I got home.
teaching.es: Una descripción neutral solo cuenta lo que cualquiera podría ver: el fregadero estaba otra vez lleno de platos cuando llegué a casa.
teaching.explanationEs: Descripción neutral: hechos comprobables, sin juicio ni emoción.
segments: A neutral description only states what anyone could see: the
sink was full of dishes again when I got home.
teaching.audioText: A neutral description only states what anyone could see: the sink was full of dishes again when I got home.

teaching.en: I feel frustrated when plans change at the last minute, because then I cannot organise my week properly.
teaching.es: Me siento frustrado cuando los planes cambian a última hora, porque entonces no puedo organizar bien mi semana.
teaching.explanationEs: Mensaje en primera persona: I feel + emoción + when + situación + because + consecuencia.
segments: I feel frustrated when plans change at the last
minute, because then I cannot organise my week properly.
teaching.audioText: I feel frustrated when plans change at the last minute, because then I cannot organise my week properly.

teaching.en: You always blame me for everything, and that sweeping accusation makes any calm conversation impossible.
teaching.es: Siempre me echas la culpa de todo, y esa acusación tan generalizada hace imposible cualquier conversación tranquila.
teaching.explanationEs: Always y everything exageran: una acusación cierra la conversación aunque tenga algo de verdad.
segments: You always blame me for everything, and that
sweeping accusation makes any calm conversation impossible.
teaching.audioText: You always blame me for everything, and that sweeping accusation makes any calm conversation impossible.

teaching.en: I feel upset whenever nobody asks for my opinion, although it is hard to say so without sounding bitter.
teaching.es: Me siento disgustado siempre que nadie me pide mi opinión, aunque es difícil decirlo sin sonar amargado.
teaching.explanationEs: Whenever = cada vez que; el mensaje nombra la emoción y el momento exacto en que aparece.
segments: I feel upset whenever nobody asks for my opinion, although
it is hard to say so without sounding bitter.
teaching.audioText: I feel upset whenever nobody asks for my opinion, although it is hard to say so without sounding bitter.

teaching.en: Behind this argument there is a real grievance: I feel ignored, and my resentment has been growing for months.
teaching.es: Detrás de esta discusión hay una queja de fondo: me siento ignorado, y mi resentimiento lleva meses creciendo.
teaching.explanationEs: La queja de fondo es lo que siente quien habla, no el reproche que dice en voz alta.
segments: Behind this argument there is a real grievance: I feel
ignored, and my resentment has been growing for months.
teaching.audioText: Behind this argument there is a real grievance: I feel ignored, and my resentment has been growing for months.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál de estas frases acusa a la otra persona en vez de describir un hecho?

choices.text: The phone rang twice during the whole dinner.
You never bother to ask how my day went.
I feel left out when dinner starts without me.

feedback.es: «You never bother…» generaliza con never y juzga a la persona: es una acusación.

hint.es: La acusación habla de lo que la otra persona «siempre» o «nunca» hace.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cada vez que intento sacar el tema del dinero, me quitas importancia.»

feedback.es: Bring up es el phrasal verb para sacar un tema en una conversación; raise no lleva up.

hint.es: Es el verbo que forma «___ up» con el significado de sacar un tema.

origin.text: Leo knows that something is wrong at home. Every time he tries to ___ up the subject of money, his father changes the subject.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me siento frustrado cuando cancelas a última hora.»

answer.text: I feel frustrated when you cancel at the last minute

feedback.es: El mensaje en primera persona sigue el orden emoción, when y situación.

hint.es: Empieza con I feel y la emoción va antes de when.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato del pódcast y elige cuál era la queja de fondo de la oyente.

choices.text: She was angry because her brother shouted back at her at the dinner table.
She was annoyed that her brother had chosen the restaurant alone.
Her news seemed to matter less to her brother than his phone.

feedback.es: La oyente dice que lo que dolía era sentir que su noticia no importaba; el móvil y los gritos son solo el detonante.

origin.audio: On a podcast about family life, a listener describes a dinner that went badly. She says her brother kept checking his phone while she talked about her new job. She told him, You always ignore me, and he shouted back that she always blamed him for everything. Looking back, she realises that the phone was not the real problem. What hurt was the feeling that her news did not matter, and that resentment had been growing for months.

prompt.es: Con el mismo relato, elige qué respondió el hermano cuando ella le acusó.

choices.text: He said that she was always blaming him for everything.
He said that she never listened when he spoke to her.
He promised to ask about her new job after dinner.

feedback.es: El hermano devuelve la acusación: «she always blamed him for everything»; no dice que ella nunca escucha ni promete nada.

origin.audio: On a podcast about family life, a listener describes a dinner that went badly. She says her brother kept checking his phone while she talked about her new job. She told him, You always ignore me, and he shouted back that she always blamed him for everything. Looking back, she realises that the phone was not the real problem. What hurt was the feeling that her news did not matter, and that resentment had been growing for months.

prompt.es: Completa: «Siempre que pone música de madrugada, Mia se siente cansada.»

feedback.es: Whenever significa «siempre que» y une la emoción con el momento en que aparece.

origin.text: Mia does not mind the music itself. ___ her flatmate plays it after midnight, she feels tired at work the next day.

prompt.es: Escucha a Sara y elige qué actitud adopta ante su padre.

choices.text: She accepts that he decides everything, but wants to say so once.
She asks firmly to be included, without accusing him of anything.
She hopes he will change the plans because she dislikes the hotel.

feedback.es: Sara nombra su emoción, reconoce que no hubo mala intención y pide participar: firme, sin acusar.

origin.audio: Sara put down her glass and looked at her father. I feel upset every time nobody asks for my opinion, she said quietly. Last week you chose the holiday dates, and on Sunday you paid for the hotel. I know you did not mean anything by it, Dad, but I would like to be part of these decisions. Her father said nothing for a moment. Then he nodded and took out the calendar.

prompt.es: Con la misma escena, elige para qué dice Sara «I know you did not mean anything by it».

choices.text: To excuse him for paying for the hotel without asking her.
To suggest that the holiday dates were a serious mistake.
To separate her feeling from any judgement about his intentions.

feedback.es: Esa frase evita que el mensaje suene a acusación: describe lo que ella siente, no lo que él pretendía.

origin.audio: Sara put down her glass and looked at her father. I feel upset every time nobody asks for my opinion, she said quietly. Last week you chose the holiday dates, and on Sunday you paid for the hotel. I know you did not mean anything by it, Dad, but I would like to be part of these decisions. Her father said nothing for a moment. Then he nodded and took out the calendar.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es una descripción neutral: cuenta lo que pasó y no juzga a nadie.»

feedback.es: Una descripción neutral se limita a hechos comprobables; no añade emoción ni reproche.

origin.text: The report says that the living room was empty at noon and that the window was open. That is a ___ description: it states what happened and judges nobody.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me siento disgustado siempre que cambian mis planes sin avisar.»

answer.text: I feel upset whenever my plans change without warning

feedback.es: Whenever sitúa el momento de la emoción justo después del mensaje I feel + emoción.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de Mia y elige qué pretende con él.

choices.text: To let him know about the problem without attacking him.
To ask him directly to turn the music down at once.
To warn him that she would complain to the landlord.

feedback.es: El mensaje solo describe hechos; Mia espera que el vecino saque la conclusión sin sentirse acusado.

origin.audio: Mia sent her neighbour a text that said: The music was still playing at two in the morning, and my window was open. She did not add a complaint or a request. Later she admitted that she hoped he would understand the message without being told what to do.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje de Leo y elige qué queja de fondo esconden sus acusaciones.

choices.text: Leo wants his sister to move out of the flat soon.
Leo feels that he carries the household work alone.
Leo is upset that his sister keeps the bathroom tidy.

feedback.es: Tras «never» y «always» Leo dice que es el único a quien le importa el piso: se siente solo con las tareas.

origin.text: Leo's message to his sister: You never wash up, and you always leave your things everywhere. I am tired of being the only one who cares about this flat.

prompt.es: Completa: «En realidad, la queja de fondo es que Tom siente que nadie nota su ayuda.»

feedback.es: La grievance es la queja de fondo: lo que realmente molesta bajo el reproche.

origin.text: Everyone thinks the argument is about the dishes. In fact, the real ___ is that Tom feels nobody notices his help.

title.es: Lo que te escucho decir es

es: Reformular lo que siente y necesita la otra persona con What I'm hearing is y It sounds like, comprobando que lo has entendido bien.

vocabulary.es: dar validez a lo que siente alguien

teaching.en: What I'm hearing is that you feel overwhelmed by the chores, and that you need more help than you are getting at the moment.
teaching.es: Lo que te estoy oyendo es que te sientes agobiado por las tareas de la casa y que necesitas más ayuda de la que estás recibiendo ahora.
teaching.explanationEs: What I'm hearing is that + emoción + necesidad: refleja sin juzgar ni defenderte.
segments: What I'm hearing is that you feel overwhelmed by the chores, and
that you need more help than you are getting at the moment.
teaching.audioText: What I'm hearing is that you feel overwhelmed by the chores, and that you need more help than you are getting at the moment.

teaching.en: It sounds like you feel left out whenever the plans are made without you, which points to an unmet need to be asked first.
teaching.es: Parece que te sientes excluido siempre que los planes se hacen sin ti, lo que apunta a una necesidad sin cubrir: que te pregunten antes.
teaching.explanationEs: It sounds like + sujeto + verbo (sin that): nombra la emoción y la necesidad que hay debajo.
segments: It sounds like you feel left out whenever the plans are made
without you, which points to an unmet need to be asked first.
teaching.audioText: It sounds like you feel left out whenever the plans are made without you, which points to an unmet need to be asked first.

teaching.en: So you need more time together, and you wish we shared the chores more evenly. Is that right?
teaching.es: Entonces necesitas más tiempo juntos y desearías que repartiéramos las tareas de forma más equitativa. ¿Es así?
teaching.explanationEs: Termina comprobando: Is that right? deja que la otra persona corrija tu lectura.
segments: So you need more time together, and you wish
we shared the chores more evenly. Is that right?
teaching.audioText: So you need more time together, and you wish we shared the chores more evenly. Is that right?

teaching.en: It sounds like you wish we had more time together, and that you feel alone even when we are all at home.
teaching.es: Parece que desearías que tuviéramos más tiempo juntos y que te sientes solo incluso cuando estamos todos en casa.
teaching.explanationEs: Wish + pasado simple: un deseo sobre algo que no es así ahora.
segments: It sounds like you wish we had more time together, and
that you feel alone even when we are all at home.
teaching.audioText: It sounds like you wish we had more time together, and that you feel alone even when we are all at home.

teaching.en: If only I had listened sooner, you would not feel so alone now, and I am sorry that I did not.
teaching.es: Ojalá te hubiera escuchado antes; ahora no te sentirías tan solo, y siento no haberlo hecho.
teaching.explanationEs: If only + pasado perfecto lamenta algo que no ocurrió; se dice con calma, sin defenderse.
segments: If only I had listened sooner, you would not feel so
alone now, and I am sorry that I did not.
teaching.audioText: If only I had listened sooner, you would not feel so alone now, and I am sorry that I did not.

teaching.en: Before I reframe your complaint, I want to validate what you feel and check that I heard you right.
teaching.es: Antes de reformular tu queja, quiero dar validez a lo que sientes y comprobar que te he entendido bien.
teaching.explanationEs: Validar una emoción no significa darle la razón en todo: significa reconocer que tiene sentido.
segments: Before I reframe your complaint, I want to validate what
you feel and check that I heard you right.
teaching.audioText: Before I reframe your complaint, I want to validate what you feel and check that I heard you right.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase refleja la emoción y la necesidad de la otra persona sin juzgar?

choices.text: What I'm hearing is that you are being unfair to everybody at home.
It sounds like you should ask for help a little more politely.
It sounds like you feel overwhelmed and need more help.

feedback.es: Solo la primera reformulación nombra una emoción y una necesidad; las otras juzgan o aconsejan.

hint.es: Busca la que nombra lo que siente la persona y lo que necesita, sin opinar.

prompt.es: Completa: «Parece que te sientes excluida y necesitas que te incluyan.»

feedback.es: It sounds like + sujeto + verbo abre la reformulación; sounds lleva -s porque el sujeto es it.

hint.es: Es el verbo que va entre It y like, con -s.

origin.text: Mia says nobody ever asks her opinion and that she eats alone while the others talk. Tom replies: It ___ like you feel left out, and you need to be included.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Lo que oigo es que te sientes agobiado.»

answer.text: What I'm hearing is that you feel overwhelmed

feedback.es: La reformulación empieza por What I'm hearing is that y nombra la emoción al final.

hint.es: Empieza con What y cierra con la emoción.

prompt.es: Escucha la escena y elige qué hace Ana en lugar de defenderse.

choices.text: She repeats what she understands about her sister's feelings and needs.
She explains why she has been working such long hours.
She offers to do all of the chores from now on, starting tonight.

feedback.es: Ana refleja la emoción (overwhelmed) y la necesidad (more help) y comprueba con Is that right?; no se justifica ni promete.

origin.audio: Ana came home late again after a long week, and her sister was waiting at the door with her arms crossed. The kitchen was a mess. You are always at work, her sister said. I do everything in this house. Instead of defending herself, Ana took a deep breath. It sounds like you feel overwhelmed by the chores, she said, and like you need more help from me. Is that right? Her sister relaxed a little. Yes, she answered. That is exactly how I feel.

prompt.es: Con la misma escena, elige qué cambia en la hermana tras «Is that right?».

choices.text: She becomes angrier because Ana interrupted her complaint.
She relaxes because she feels that Ana has heard her.
She decides to leave the house until Ana stops working.

feedback.es: La hermana se relaja y confirma «That is exactly how I feel»: al sentirse escuchada, baja la tensión.

origin.audio: Ana came home late again after a long week, and her sister was waiting at the door with her arms crossed. The kitchen was a mess. You are always at work, her sister said. I do everything in this house. Instead of defending herself, Ana took a deep breath. It sounds like you feel overwhelmed by the chores, she said, and like you need more help from me. Is that right? Her sister relaxed a little. Yes, she answered. That is exactly how I feel.

prompt.es: Completa: «Parece que desearías que tuviéramos más tiempo juntos.»

feedback.es: Wish va seguido de pasado simple (had) cuando hablamos de un deseo sobre el presente.

origin.text: Leo says that he is fine, but he eats dinner alone every evening. Mia tells him: It sounds like you wish we ___ more time together.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué Leo se queda en silencio un segundo.

choices.text: He is thinking of a good way to answer the accusation without delay.
He is angry because his flatmate did not understand him.
He is surprised that someone has put his feeling into words.

feedback.es: Leo confirma «That is exactly it»: el silencio refleja sorpresa al ver su emoción nombrada, no enfado.

origin.audio: When Leo said that nobody ever asked him anything, his flatmate did not answer with an excuse. He said, What I'm hearing is that you feel left out, and that you need to be consulted before decisions are made. Leo was silent for a second. Then he said quietly, That is exactly it, but I did not know how to say it.

prompt.es: Con el mismo relato, elige con qué fin usa el compañero «What I'm hearing is...».

choices.text: To check that he has understood Leo's feeling and need.
To tell Leo that he should ask for what he wants.
To explain why nobody consulted Leo about the decisions.

feedback.es: La fórmula sirve para devolver lo oído y comprobarlo, no para aconsejar ni justificarse.

origin.audio: When Leo said that nobody ever asked him anything, his flatmate did not answer with an excuse. He said, What I'm hearing is that you feel left out, and that you need to be consulted before decisions are made. Leo was silent for a second. Then he said quietly, That is exactly it, but I did not know how to say it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Reformula la queja como una necesidad: necesito más ayuda con las tareas.»

feedback.es: Reframe es presentar la misma queja desde otro ángulo: pasar del reproche a la necesidad.

origin.text: Instead of telling your brother that he is lazy, try to ___ the complaint as a need: I need more help with the chores.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Parece que te sientes solo y necesitas más apoyo.»

answer.text: It sounds like you feel alone and need more support

feedback.es: Después de It sounds like va un sujeto y un verbo: you feel alone and need...

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje de voz de Tom y elige la respuesta que refleja lo que siente sin juzgar.

choices.text: It sounds like you want a medal, and you need more attention from us.
It sounds like you feel overwhelmed, and you need someone to notice your effort.
What I'm hearing is that the others are lazy, and you are right to complain.

feedback.es: La reformulación nombra agobio y necesidad de reconocimiento; las otras leen mal a Tom o toman partido.

origin.text: Tom's voice message: I've been doing the washing, the shopping and the bins all week, and nobody has said a word. I'm not asking for a medal, but it would be nice if someone noticed. Honestly, I'm exhausted.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender el hermano con su frase.

choices.text: That he wants to finish the dinner earlier than planned.
That he is annoyed because she keeps looking at the clock.
That he has read her real feeling behind her polite words.

feedback.es: El hermano lee lo que hay detrás de «I'm fine»; Mia lo confirma con «That is right».

origin.audio: Mia says she is fine, but her voice is flat and she keeps looking at the clock. Her brother thinks for a moment and says: It sounds like you wish you were somewhere else tonight. Mia laughs, relieved. That is right, she says, I did not want to come to this dinner.

prompt.es: Completa: «Antes de explicar mi versión, quiero dar validez a lo que sientes.»

feedback.es: Validate significa reconocer que lo que siente la otra persona tiene sentido, sin exigir que estés de acuerdo en todo.

origin.text: Anyone would feel left out in that situation. Before I explain my side, I want to ___ how you feel.

es: Decidir si un diálogo tenso se agrava o se repara y localizar la frase que marca el cambio: sarcasmo, interrupciones, tono, reconocimiento y disculpa.

teaching.en: Please don't interrupt me; I would like to finish my point before you answer, and then I will listen to yours.
teaching.es: Por favor, no me interrumpas; me gustaría terminar mi idea antes de que contestes, y luego escucharé la tuya.
teaching.explanationEs: Interrumpir y hablar por encima del otro es una señal de que la discusión se agrava.
segments: Please don't interrupt me; I would like to finish my point
before you answer, and then I will listen to yours.
teaching.audioText: Please don't interrupt me; I would like to finish my point before you answer, and then I will listen to yours.

teaching.en: Oh, brilliant, you forgot again: that sarcastic comment will only escalate the argument and make everyone more defensive.
teaching.es: Oh, genial, se te olvidó otra vez: ese comentario sarcástico solo agravará la discusión y pondrá a todos más a la defensiva.
teaching.explanationEs: El sarcasmo dice lo contrario de lo que siente y hiere; provoca que el otro se ponga a la defensiva.
segments: Oh, brilliant, you forgot again: that sarcastic comment will
only escalate the argument and make everyone more defensive.
teaching.audioText: Oh, brilliant, you forgot again: that sarcastic comment will only escalate the argument and make everyone more defensive.

teaching.en: That was a snide remark, and I would rather you were direct, because your tone is hurting me more than your words.
teaching.es: Eso fue un comentario malicioso, y preferiría que fueras directo, porque tu tono me hiere más que tus palabras.
teaching.explanationEs: El tono importa tanto como las palabras: se puede señalar con calma.
segments: That was a snide remark, and I would rather you were
direct, because your tone is hurting me more than your words.
teaching.audioText: That was a snide remark, and I would rather you were direct, because your tone is hurting me more than your words.

teaching.en: Fair point: I was getting defensive and trying to deflect the blame, and I am sorry about that.
teaching.es: Buen punto: me estaba poniendo a la defensiva y trataba de desviar la culpa, y lo siento.
teaching.explanationEs: Fair point reconoce lo razonable de la otra persona; deflect es desviar la culpa en vez de asumirla.
segments: Fair point: I was getting defensive and trying to
deflect the blame, and I am sorry about that.
teaching.audioText: Fair point: I was getting defensive and trying to deflect the blame, and I am sorry about that.

teaching.en: Let's take a break and come back in twenty minutes, when we are both calmer and ready to repair this.
teaching.es: Hagamos una pausa y volvamos en veinte minutos, cuando los dos estemos más tranquilos y listos para arreglar esto.
teaching.explanationEs: Proponer una pausa baja la tensión; repair es el verbo de arreglar una relación.
segments: Let's take a break and come back in twenty minutes,
when we are both calmer and ready to repair this.
teaching.audioText: Let's take a break and come back in twenty minutes, when we are both calmer and ready to repair this.

teaching.en: After weeks of hostile silence, her offer to cook dinner felt like an olive branch that he was happy to accept.
teaching.es: Tras semanas de silencio hostil, su ofrecimiento de cocinar la cena fue como un gesto de paz que él aceptó encantado.
teaching.explanationEs: An olive branch es un gesto que busca la paz después de un conflicto.
segments: After weeks of hostile silence, her offer to cook dinner felt
like an olive branch that he was happy to accept.
teaching.audioText: After weeks of hostile silence, her offer to cook dinner felt like an olive branch that he was happy to accept.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase agrava la discusión en lugar de repararla?

choices.text: Oh, great, you forgot again. What a surprise.
Fair point. I forgot, and I am sorry.
Let's take a break and talk later.

feedback.es: El sarcasmo de «Oh, great» dice lo contrario de lo que siente y hiere: agrava la discusión.

hint.es: Busca la frase que dice lo contrario de lo que siente.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tom intentó desviar la culpa hablando de otra cosa.»

feedback.es: Deflect the blame significa desviar la culpa hacia otro tema o persona en lugar de asumirla.

hint.es: Es el verbo para apartar la culpa de uno mismo.

origin.text: When Sara asked who had left the door open, Tom tried to ___ the blame by talking about something else.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Buen punto, estaba a la defensiva y lo siento.»

answer.text: Fair point I was defensive and I am sorry

feedback.es: La reparación suma reconocimiento, admisión de la propia parte y disculpa breve.

hint.es: Empieza por Fair point y termina con la disculpa.

prompt.es: Escucha la escena y elige quién da el primer paso hacia la reparación y cómo.

choices.text: Tom, by apologising for looking at the ceiling while she was talking.
Mia, by lowering her voice and saying how she feels.
Mia, by suggesting that they take a break together.

feedback.es: Mia baja la voz y habla de su emoción; Tom reconoce su parte después, y es él quien propone la pausa.

origin.audio: Mia and Tom were arguing about the washing-up. You always leave it for me, Mia said. Tom looked at the ceiling and answered, Oh, brilliant, here we go again. Mia stopped, took a breath and lowered her voice. I don't want to fight, she said. When you look at the ceiling while I talk, I feel ignored. Tom was silent, then he nodded. Fair point, he said. I was being defensive. Shall we take a break and look at the rota together?

prompt.es: Con la misma escena, elige con qué fin dice Mia que se siente ignorada.

choices.text: To accuse Tom of never taking her seriously.
To ask Tom to leave the room until he is calm.
To point at a behaviour and say how it affects her.

feedback.es: Mia describe un gesto y su efecto en ella, sin generalizar; por eso la escalada se detiene.

origin.audio: Mia and Tom were arguing about the washing-up. You always leave it for me, Mia said. Tom looked at the ceiling and answered, Oh, brilliant, here we go again. Mia stopped, took a breath and lowered her voice. I don't want to fight, she said. When you look at the ceiling while I talk, I feel ignored. Tom was silent, then he nodded. Fair point, he said. I was being defensive. Shall we take a break and look at the rota together?

prompt.es: Completa: «Lo que dolió no fue lo que dijo, sino su tono: plano, frío e impaciente.»

feedback.es: El tono puede herir más que las palabras: lo que suena frío o impaciente escala el conflicto.

origin.text: Nobody complained about his words. It was his ___ that hurt: flat, cold and impatient.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato y elige qué se puede deducir de cómo terminó la discusión.

choices.text: It ended without repair, and the tension stayed in the house.
It ended well because Sara finally understood what her father meant by his tone.
It ended when her father apologised for the dirty car.

feedback.es: Nadie habla esa noche y Sara escribe sobre el tono: no hubo reparación, la tensión continúa.

origin.audio: Sara's father asked why the car was dirty again. It is always my fault, she snapped. Well, you never say thank you for anything, he replied, and he left the room. The door closed loudly. Neither of them spoke that evening. Later Sara wrote in her diary that the real problem was not the car, but the tone of the conversation.

prompt.es: Con el mismo relato, elige por qué fracasó la conversación según Sara.

choices.text: Because her father refused to talk about the dirty car with her at all.

origin.text: Some people think that a mediator decides who is right. In fact, a good mediator does not ___ sides: she helps both people find a solution.

prompt.es: Escribe el mensaje final de la mediación a Ana y Leo.

answer.text:
Dear Ana and Leo,
Thank you both for talking so openly today. Let me summarise what I heard. Ana, it sounds like you feel overwhelmed when the Sunday plans change at the last minute, and you need to know earlier. Leo, what I'm hearing is that you feel left out when you cannot see your friends, and you need some free time. Neither of you is wrong: you both want a calm weekend and to feel respected.
What if we try a compromise? Leo will tell Ana by Friday evening if he has other plans. Ana will keep Sunday lunch free until then, and she will not ask him to cancel later. If either of you feels upset, please say it with an I-message, for example, I feel frustrated when...
So we agreed that we will follow this plan for two weeks. Let's review it next Sunday, and we can change anything that does not work.
Thank you both for your honesty and your patience. I am proud of how you listened to each other.
Mia

Hi Ana and Leo,
I'm glad we talked. To summarise: Ana, it sounds like you feel stressed because the plans for Sunday lunch change suddenly, and you need time to organise. Leo, it sounds like you feel frustrated because you rarely see your friends, and you need space. I think you both want the same thing, which is a peaceful home where everybody feels heard.
Could we agree on a simple solution? Leo will tell Ana by Friday whether he is free on Sunday. In return, Ana will not plan the lunch until she hears from him. If there is a problem, we will speak calmly and take a break first.
So we agreed that this starts this week. We will check in again in two weeks, and then we will decide if we keep it.
Thanks for listening to each other. I'm proud of both of you, and I hope that the plan makes Sundays calmer and happier for everybody in the family. If either of you feels upset before then, please say it with an I-message and we will talk.
Mia

feedback.es: «Slightly unhappy but respected» resume la idea: en un buen compromiso cada parte cede algo sin perder el respeto.

origin.audio: After two hours of arguing, the brother and sister finally agreed on a plan. Nobody won completely: she gave up her Sunday dinners twice a month, and he promised to call every Friday. The mediator said that a good compromise leaves both people slightly unhappy but respected.

prompt.es: Completa: «Un mediador debe ser imparcial: si toma partido, nadie confiará en ella.»

feedback.es: Impartial describe a quien no favorece a ninguna parte; sin imparcialidad, el mediador pierde la confianza.

origin.text: A mediator must stay ___. If she takes sides, nobody will trust her.
